models_note: The gen-4 runs are ONE experiment, not four models: the same corpus (all 20 stores, 336,000 deals) and the same evaluation, with a small number of ingredients changed per run. The numbers are the plan's order, not the order they ran — Jerry reordered execution to 1 -> 4 -> 3 -> 2 on 2026-09-21 so the objective was tested before depth. Run 1 is the baseline: gen-3-warm's recipe (residual trunk d4, JS-M1 warm start) on the bigger corpus with HARD targets, the played action as the policy label. Run 4 changes exactly one thing against it, the objective: SOFT targets, the search's own per-candidate values. Runs 2 and 3 are ALSO soft, so the reference for them is RUN 4, not run 1: run 2 changes capacity (residual trunk at depth 6 instead of 4) and run 3 changes architecture AND warm start together (a grid trunk, depth 3 and 44 channels, started from JS-G1 instead of JS-M1). So run 1 vs run 4 isolates the objective, run 4 vs run 2 isolates depth, and run 4 vs run 3 moves two things at once — which is why run 3's read is not attributable to a single ingredient.
head_ladder_note: Policy head ALONE: each head plays every card decision by argmax of its summed card log-odds over the capped legal set, no value net, no rollouts, heuristic declare/bury, 8,000 mirrored deals (seed0 20000, the 09-18 ladder's harness). 'vs SmartBot' is the ladder; 'vs production head' is a PAIRED duel of two heads on the same deals, the release-30 head (8ecd4fea) scored by the identical rule (its self-duel reads exactly 0). Standard for every exported model from 2026-09-30. These measure the admission head alone; the served search (which the value head decides) is what the screens read. A better head alone is not a better served bot: PBF1 reads +0.238 vs the production head (paired vs SMV3 +0.031 [+0.015,+0.048]) yet served v39a reads -0.0525 [-0.0878,-0.0171] vs release 36.
